claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy-alloy coating containing coherent nanoprecipitates will reduce erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum relative to conventional materials.
A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy can be engineered with stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations.
The proposed material is a bulk alloy.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA can be applied as a protective coating to rollers and guide plates.
The coating is intended to withstand long-term molten-aluminum exposure under cyclic thermal loads.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote formation of a stable protective oxide scale.
Coherent nanoprecipitates enhance the mechanical integrity of tungsten-based refractory HEAs.
The proposed HEA will form a robust protective oxide layer at the hot-dip operating temperature.
The protective oxide layer will inhibit liquid-aluminum penetration and corrosion.
The coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
The coherent-nanoprecipitation design provides high strength at elevated temperature.
The nanoprecipitates mitigate dislocation-driven degradation during molten-aluminum exposure.
The oxide scale and nanoprecipitate-strengthening mechanisms will reduce erosion by molten aluminum.
Coated parts will have significantly lower erosion rates than uncoated or conventionally coated parts during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.
Coated parts will retain greater structural stability during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.
Traditional dipping and plating equipment materials undergo accelerated corrosion and material loss in direct contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The proposed protective effect applies under steady high-temperature hot-dip conditions.

contradictions.description: The conditions place the prediction under cyclic thermal loads, whereas the boundary limits the predicted protective effect to steady high-temperature conditions and says thermal-cycling performance remains unestablished.
